text:
[verdict]
In the 50 retrieved episodes where the tape looked like this, SPY and its analogs produced a median 5-session return of -0.1% with a standard deviation of 2.14%. The distribution is nearly symmetric but slightly right-skewed at 0.51, meaning the upside tail is marginally fatter than the downside. The single number to anchor on for path risk is the median max adverse excursion of -1.05%, which describes how far underwater these trades typically went before the 5 sessions were up.

[state]
The current state as of 2026-09-18 is defined by three notable extremes that pull specific historical episodes into the neighborhood. First, the 20-session dollar-volume regime z-score (dv20z) sits at -1.985, indicating unusually thin liquidity. Second, WTI crude change over 20 days (oilChg20) is 19.24%, a sharp energy move. Third, 20-session realised volatility (vol20) is compressed at 9.16%. Supporting features include a distance from the 52-week high (dist52) of -2.27%, a 5d/20d volatility ratio (volRatio) of 1.192, and a mean absolute overnight/weekend gap (gap20) of 0.37%. The engine weighted these using a feature group structure: name-level price/vol features at 30%, broad market context at 20%, macro at 20%, event timing at 20%, and crypto at 10%. This combination of low volume, an oil shock, and compressed volatility retrieves a set dominated by recent broad ETF sessions—18 of the 50 analogs are ETF Broad names, with 26 drawn from 2025 and 14 from 2026.

[history]
Across the 50 analogs, the 5-session forward returns range from -5.12% to 6.88%. The interquartile spread runs from -1.31% at the 25th percentile to 0.92% at the 75th percentile. Exactly 52% of the episodes finished below zero, while 48% finished above it. The histogram shows the bulk of outcomes clustered between -0.87% and 1.13%, with the largest single bin at 0.13% holding 14% of the observations. The bad tail is populated by specific recent episodes. The closest match is IWM on 2026-09-08 (distance 0.2997), which returned -2.98% over 5 sessions. SPY itself appears in the top matches: on 2026-09-03 (distance 0.3101) it returned -1.15%, and on 2016-12-14 (distance 0.3324) it returned 0.54%. JPM on 2026-09-04 (distance 0.3418) delivered -2.37%, and DIA on 2026-09-02 (distance 0.3258) fell -1.86%. Conversely, SPY on 2025-06-20 (distance 0.3366) rallied 3.47%, showing the upside tail is also active. The conformal interval, scaled at 1.31 and fitted on 2019-2022 data, spans from -2.91% to 2.7% with a width of 5.61%, achieving 80.8% out-of-sample coverage on 2698 test queries.

[tails]
A position can end near flat and still be un-holdable if the intra-horizon drawdown forces an exit. In these 50 analogs, the median max adverse excursion was -1.05%. At the 25th percentile, the worst intra-period dip reached -1.98%, and at the 10th percentile it hit -3.1%. On the favorable side, the median max favorable excursion was 0.99%, reaching 1.89% at the 75th percentile and 3.52% at the 90th percentile, yielding a reward-risk ratio of 0.94. Looking at hard drawdown thresholds, the probability of breaching a 5% drawdown during the 5 sessions was 4%. The probability of breaching a 10%, 15%, or 20% drawdown was 0% across all retrieved episodes. For endpoint risk, the 90% value-at-risk is 2.39%, and the conditional VaR at the same level is 3.55%. Only 2% of the 50 analogs finished worse than -5%, and none finished worse than -10%.

[stress]
Stress scenarios isolate what happens when the baseline state collides with a known regime shock. The 2020-02/03 liquidity crash scenario produces the most severe deterioration: the median 5-session return drops to -4.61%, which is -4.51% worse than the baseline, and the p10 falls to -11.63%. The probability of breaching a 10% drawdown jumps to 41.7%. However, central-bank backstops arrived inside the window, so the realised rebound is baked into the forward returns; it is a sample of one regime, not a forecast of the next one. The 2025-04 tariff shock scenario yields a median of -0.92% (-0.82% vs baseline) with a p10 of -11.26% and a 23.1% probability of a 10% drawdown, though policy reversals inside the window make the tail asymmetric in a way specific to that episode. The 2022 inflation/rate bear scenario gives a median of -2.09% (-1.99% vs baseline) and a p10 of -5.01%; treat it as a regime description rather than 50 independent events because the nine-month window samples dates repeatedly under a per-date cap of 2. The 2018-Q4 tightening scare shows a median of -1.09% (-0.99% vs baseline) and a p10 of -4.75%, but it ended with a policy pivot in January 2019, which flatters the forward returns of late-window analogs. The 2024-08-05 carry unwind delivers a median of -0.49% (-0.39% vs baseline) with a p10 of -4.04%; the reversal was almost as fast as the drawdown, so H-day forward returns look benign even though the intra-horizon excursion did not. The earnings release day shock shows a median of -0.79% (-0.69% vs baseline) and a p10 of -6.71%, but earnings dates for foreign private issuers come from 6-K full-text search and are noisier than domestic 8-K Item 2.02 dates. The volatility spike (+2 sigma VIX) scenario yields a median of -0.2% (-0.1% vs baseline) with a p10 of -4.18%; VIX shocks mean-revert quickly, so this stresses entry timing more than terminal value. The liquidity air pocket scenario gives a median of -0.13% (-0.03% vs baseline) and a p10 of -4.2%, but gap20 is measured on the underlying exchange session, bounding reference-market gap risk only. Scenarios that actually improved the picture versus baseline include the 2023-03 regional bank stress (median 1.41%, +1.51% vs baseline), though the very short window means the analog set is dominated by a handful of sessions, and crypto drawdown contagion (median 0.77%, +0.87% vs baseline), though the BTC feature is a market-wide proxy and any name-level linkage to crypto flows is not identified here. Policy-rate path re-pricing, FOMC decision day, and China ADR de-rating scenarios produced medians within 0.26% of the baseline. No scenarios were skipped by the engine.

[limits]
This analysis has concrete limits. The engine's own validation states explicitly: "Analog retrieval hits its coverage target out of sample and its width tracks each instrument's own volatility, but it is NOT sharper than a same-name unconditional band at matched coverage, and its raw PIT distribution fails a uniformity test. It is a stress-testing and provenance instrument, not an alpha source." Specifically, the matched coverage sharpness versus the same-name unconditional benchmark is -7.6%, meaning the naive benchmark is tighter. The raw probability integral transform chi-square statistic is 208.6 against a 5% critical value of 16.92, confirming the failure of uniformity. The directional hit rate is 50.1%. The dataset spans 2513 sessions across 71 symbols from 2016-09-20 to 2026-09-18, but prices are sourced keyless from api.stockanalysis.com and earnings from SEC full-text search, introducing noise. The retrieval found 50 analogs but only 28 distinct sessions and 22 distinct symbols, with just 7 being SPY itself, meaning the results rely heavily on cross-sectional proxies like IWM, QQQ, and UUP rather than pure SPY history.
